To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel approach for the automated inference of phosphorylation-dependent gene regulatory networks from phosphoproteomics and transcriptomics data, and that this method has the potential to identify novel genes that are involved in the regulation of the phosphorylation of a given phosphoprotein of interest.
the TILAR algorithm is capable of inferring predictive phospho-regulatory networks from LC-MS MS data and that the resulting network models are able to predict novel phospho-regulatory interactions.

the proposed approach for the automated inference of phospho-regulatory networks from LC-MSMS phosphoproteomics datasets can successfully identify novel phospho-regulatory interactions and can be used to generate testable hypotheses about the function of novel phospho-regulated proteins in the cellular signaling machinery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automated inference of phospho-regulatory networks from LC-MS phosphoproteomics and RNA-seq transcriptomics data.
the development and evaluation of a novel network inference method for the analysis of LC-MS/ MS based phosphoproteomics datasets.
the development of methods for the automated inference of phosphoproteome networks and their application to the analysis of LC-MS/ MS phosphoproteomics datasets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TILAR is able to infer biologically relevant phosphopredictive networks from phosphoproteomics datasets.
the TILAR method is able to infer predictive networks for phospho-regulatory data.
the TILAR algorithm is a promising approach for the inference of predictive phospho-regulatory networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to show that the TILAR algorithm can be used for the inference of predictive phosphorylation-related regulatory networks from phosphoproteomics datasets.
we have successfully adapted a well established gene regulatory network inference algorithm for use with LC-MS/ MS phosphoproteomics datasets.
we have developed a novel network inference approach to predict the regulatory mechanisms that govern the phosphorylation of proteins in response to external stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the integration of diverse sources of information is essential for the identification of biologically relevant phosphorylation events and for the inference of predictive phosphorylation regulatory networks.

it is possible to automatically infer biologically meaningful phosphoregulatory networks from phosphoproteomics datasets, which are not only able to explain the observed data but also provide a basis for the prediction of novel phosphorylation sites.
we have shown that it is feasible to infer predictive phosphorylation networks from phosphoproteomics experiments, and we provide a first proof of concept.
